meta.title: Why you can never step in the same river twice

plates.query: J. M. W. Turner river landscape sunset painting
plates.want: Turner, a moving river of light (PD)

beats.text: You step into a river. You step in again a moment later. Same river, surely?
Heraclitus said no. The water you first touched is already gone, carried downstream.
"You cannot step twice into the same river," he wrote. The river is only its flowing.
And neither are you the same. Your cells, your moods, your mind — all of it is moving too.
Nothing stands still. Everything flows. What looks solid is just change that is slow enough to miss.
We suffer when we grip the water and demand it stay. It never will.
Stop clutching the river. Learn, instead, to swim.
